proposed_partner_narrative_block.headline: DiDi can connect the ride to the ramp in Chile and Argentina—starting where official city coverage and real passenger-water infrastructure overlap.
proposed_partner_narrative_block.body: The strongest source-backed openings are Punta Arenas/Tres Puentes, Valdivia’s Niebla–Corral gateway, Puerto Montt’s broader Chiloé access system, Buenos Aires/Tigre’s public delta network, Rosario’s seasonal island crossing and Bariloche’s lake-excursion ports. DiDi city evidence is exact only for the named official cities; nearby ferry towns and island endpoints remain regional candidates until service polygons are verified.
proof_points: Chile official list names six prioritized coastal/river anchors.
Argentina official list names Buenos Aires, Rosario and Bariloche.
Operators and authorities verify real terminals and routes; no Atlas IDs currently exist for either country.
The Tigre network already behaves like a multi-branch water-transit mesh, but requires hand-routed geometry through rivers and channels.
guardrails: Do not imply DiDi operates in Porvenir, Corral, Calbuco, Chacao, Dalcahue, Lota, Tigre or island endpoints without app/service-polygon proof.
Do not call Muelle Prat a scheduled transit corridor.
Do not present seasonal Rosario service as year-round.
Do not present Buenos Aires–Colonia as an ordinary domestic route; it is international.

partner_narrative_notes.canonical_brief_rule: All eventual Atlas briefs remain partner-neutral. DiDi-specific dispatch, first/last-mile and in-app framing belongs only in partner proposal copy.

gaps.next_action: Approve country/cluster/city hierarchy candidates for Chile and Argentina; assign final IDs only after review.
Obtain authoritative coordinates for every candidate ramp/landing and hand-route all braided river, channel and lake paths; run land-crossing QA.
Verify app/service polygons for Niebla, Calbuco/Pargua/Chacao/Dalcahue, Lota/Talcahuano and Tigre; city-list evidence alone is insufficient for nearby municipalities.
Request annual one-way passenger counts and route-level fare tables from TABSA, RVC/Puelche/Transmarchilay, Tigre/Interisleña, ENAPRO, Bariloche operators and Buquebus.
After registry approval, build partner-neutral briefs field-by-field with official demand, seasonality, regulator and competitive-service sources.
Separate Buenos Aires–Colonia for immigration/customs/cabotage/certification review before any Navier-operable claim.
Confirm current scheduled passenger use at Muelle Blanco Talcahuano and identify any explicit endpoints; otherwise keep it out of BP registry.
Confirm next summer’s Isla Sabino Corsi start date, fare, operator and landing coordinate; current page says non-summer service is suspended.

do_not_publish: No proposed slug, city label, BP label or corridor key in this artifact is a final registry ID.
Do not mint route_id values. No candidate endpoint pair matched an existing canonical ROUTES.json route; every route_id is null.
Do not infer DiDi coverage at ferry endpoints from the nearest named DiDi city.
Do not convert a city tourism count, airport flow or metro population into annual_one_way_pax.
Do not publish Muelle Blanco as a passenger BP until current operator/timetable/destination evidence is found.
Do not publish Muelle Prat bay excursions as a point-to-point transport corridor.
Do not publish Rosario–Isla Sabino Corsi as year-round service.
Do not assign vessel/platform class from elapsed ferry duration alone.
Do not render straight geodesics through Tigre Delta islands, Corral Bay shoreline, Chiloé channels, or Nahuel Huapi peninsulas.
Do not treat Puerto Madero–Colonia as domestic or deployment-ready without cross-border review.
